claims.claim: Hesychius of Jerusalem was a Christian priest (presbyter) of the Church of Jerusalem.
Hesychius of Jerusalem was active during the first half of the fifth century, and according to Theophanes Confessor became presbyter at Jerusalem in 412.
Hesychius of Jerusalem died around 450, though this date is uncertain.
Hesychius of Jerusalem was renowned as a theologian, biblical commentator, and preacher in the Eastern Church.
Hesychius of Jerusalem composed Homily 13, On Peter and Paul (CPG 6577 = BHG 1501f), which he preached during the feast of Peter and Paul on 28 December in Jerusalem.
The homily was written in Greek at Jerusalem in the early 5th century.
The homily is an encomium (praise speech) on the holy apostles Peter and Paul.
The homily's content includes praise of Peter and an account of Paul's conversion from persecutor to apostle.
Hesychius of Jerusalem played a prominent role in the 5th-century controversy on the nature of Christ.
Hesychius of Jerusalem was acclaimed as having annotated the whole of sacred Scripture.
By 429, Hesychius was recognized by chroniclers and the Orthodox Mēnologion as the pre-eminent biblical interpreter and teacher of the church in Jerusalem and Palestine.
